questions.question_text: If $\sin\theta = -\dfrac{8}{17}$ and $\cos\theta = \dfrac{15}{17}$, what is the value of $\cot\theta$?

options.why: Calculated $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ instead of $\cot\theta=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$.
Dropped the negative sign resulting from the negative sine ratio.
Evaluated $\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\frac{1}{\sin\theta}$ instead of cotangent.
Confused cotangent with tangent, which would give $\tan\theta\cos\theta=\sin\theta$.
Replaced the product with a reciprocal ratio instead of cancelling sine.
Treated $\cot\theta$ and $\sin\theta$ as reciprocals of each other.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is equivalent to $\tan\phi \operatorname{cosec}\phi$?

options.why: Inverted the fraction arriving at cosine rather than secant.
Assumed multiplying tangent and cosecant produces cotangent.
Multiplied sine terms instead of cancelling them.

questions.question_text: Which angles in the interval $-180^{\circ} \le x \le 180^{\circ}$ must be excluded from the identity $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$?

options.why: Identified where $\sin x = 0$ (the excluded angles for $\cot x$) rather than where $\cos x = 0$.
Excluded all quadrantal points in the interval instead of only where cosine is zero.
Omitted the negative solution at $-90^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ is undefined when $\cos x = 0$.
In $[-180^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}]$, $\cos x = 0$ at $x = -90^{\circ}, 90^{\circ}$.

options.why: Inverted the fraction resulting in $\frac{1}{\sin\alpha} = \operatorname{cosec}\alpha$ instead of $\sin\alpha$.
Multiplied the numerators instead of dividing by the fraction.
Omitted the cosine factor in the numerator resulting in $\frac{1}{\cot\alpha} = \tan\alpha$.

questions.question_text: If $\sin\beta = \dfrac{20}{29}$ and $\cos\beta = -\dfrac{21}{29}$, what is the value of $\tan\beta$?

options.why: Evaluated $\cot\beta=\frac{\cos\beta}{\sin\beta}$ instead of $\tan\beta=\frac{\sin\beta}{\cos\beta}$.
Omitted the negative sign from the second quadrant cosine.
Evaluated $\sec\beta=\frac{1}{\cos\beta}$ instead of tangent.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\dfrac{\cot x}{\sec x}$ in terms of primary trigonometric functions.

options.why: Inverted the fraction ratio upside down.
Cancelled cosine terms instead of multiplying them.
Dropped the $\cos^2 x$ numerator entirely.

questions.solution_text: $\dfrac{\cot x}{\sec x} = \dfrac{\cos x/\sin x}{1/\cos x} = \dfrac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}$

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly proves the identity $\tan\theta + \cot\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$?

options.why: Swapped the definitions of $\tan$ and $\cot$, and wrote subtraction in the numerator.
Multiplied the terms instead of adding them.
Added numerators and denominators across fractions without finding a common denominator.
